# Full welcome specification used in the isolated evaluation

Source: FI3-295's recorded proposed specification, read through the task record. Its closing answers copy=orientation and race=skip are authoritative over proposal defaults and unresolved prose. The historical agreement explicitly approved design only. The evaluation adds a fictional later Build it request; it does not authorize any historical task. Autonomy is off and no merge permission is supplied.

## Intent

Plan an immediate, approved, host-presented Firstmate welcome after first usable model setup. The original proposal's two questions were compact orientation versus task-first copy (recommended compact orientation), and skip versus retain an uncreated welcome when first input wins a recovery race (recommended skip). Agreement approved the specification only, not implementation.

## Complete specification

Presentation and exact copy: Create one approved Firstmate-voice note titled “Welcome aboard”, with ordinary note chrome, close and reply controls, normal note priority, and no footer actions. The one-off informational introduction is explicitly allowed to remain a note despite its starter suggestion; other cards keep the ordinary decision/action rule. Do not personalize its copy with provider/account names.

Question 1, compact orientation, exact paragraph order:
“Tell me what you want to do; I’ll bring back answers and choices as cards.”
“Crewmates do the work in the background and report to Activity on the left.”
“Every ask has a record in Tasks on the right.”
“Start with a project to clone, a new project, or a folder already on your Mac.”

Question 1 alternative, task-first, exact paragraph order:
“Tell me what you want to do; I’ll bring back answers and choices as cards.”
“Start with a project to clone, a new project, or a folder already on your Mac.”

Both versions follow those paragraphs with the same token-styled conceptual drawing: left box “Activity” / “Crew reports”, center accented box “Firstmate” / “Answers and choices”, right box “Tasks” / “Your asks”. Its exact caption is “These panels appear as work starts.” The drawing teaches the default layout; it does not claim empty panels are already visible, open panels, or override panel choices. The task-first version carries Activity/Tasks orientation in that drawing rather than extra paragraphs.

Timing: In the normal eligible fresh-setup path, commit the note before publishing the ready screen; present it alongside the newly enabled input. No welcome-composition inference, ordinary wake grouping, successful live answer, quiet-period wait or caption-fade completion is required. When another card is shown, keep it shown and add the welcome unread behind it. Preserve drafts, input focus, voice state, existing card priority and notification policy; do not raise a window or add a special alert. “Immediate” is an ordering/work contract, not a new guessed millisecond budget.

Usable-model eligibility: Use Firstmate’s existing local serving/preflight facts for the actual selected model, or its normal initial automatic selection, including provider role, serving account/binding, enablement and required client. Do not silently replace a pinned model or qualify merely because some unrelated account exists. A closed setup gate is insufficient because a known paused account can keep it closed. Cancelled/failed setup, no served model, disabled account, missing client and known allowance/auth pause do not create the note. Unknown allowance is not zero. No paid health probe is added and successful inference is not a prerequisite. Unexpected subsequent model/session failure remains an ordinary provider failure, not a reason to reissue the welcome. A supported local seat qualifies only for an already eligible pending setup.

Durable lifecycle: At initialization of new app data under the new behavior, persist pending eligibility only when setup initially needs a model. Fresh already-configured starts remain skipped, matching the existing no-gate-open behavior. Record skipped/consumed states durably; an in-memory open-to-closed edge is not the source of truth. Before an introduction has been created, prior captain activity, tasks, cards or a user-registered project exclude it under the chosen skip policy; the built-in personal workspace is not prior user activity. Existing installations are skipped conservatively even without an old welcome stamp. Preserve old timestamps and existing open/resolved welcome cards; never reconstruct a missing legacy welcome whose stamp meant only wake scheduling.

Reconcile pending state at boot and after account sign-in/add/remove/enablement, serving/auth/client changes, settled catalogs, typed quota pauses/recovery and local-seat changes. Startup can create the welcome when readiness changed while the app was closed. Reads and ready-state publication must not bypass reconciliation and expose a normal fresh-ready state before its committed note. Remove the new-install live-authored welcome request rather than supplementing it. Retire obsolete typed welcome inbox requests only, preserving unrelated queued work and existing legacy cards.

Atomic creation and recovery: Through existing single-writer services and a reusable atomic/publish seam, one transaction creates the note, the existing-style completed standalone answer record, its identity and the terminal consumed marker. No active/sample task, project work or crewmate is launched. Broadcast only after commit. For new notes, the welcome timestamp means committed creation, not display/read acknowledgement; keep legacy values compatible and do not reinterpret them as proof of viewing. A stable card ID alone is insufficient because the current service can reopen resolved IDs. Before commit, pending survives and can retry; after commit, restart restores the same open card and thread. Dismissal, card cleanup, copy revision, account reconnection and upgrade never clear consumed state or automatically recreate it. This promises at most one automatic creation for an eligible profile, not exactly one viewing or proof that the user read it.

Failure and first-input races: Failed/cancelled setup keeps pending and uses existing setup/error handling. Welcome storage failure must leave no consumed marker without its note and must not disable otherwise usable input. Retry on the next serving-state reconciliation or restart, subject to question 2. Serialize accepted captain input and welcome creation into one durable event order. Never delay, reject, rewrite or co-batch the ask for the welcome. If creation wins, retain that one note, even if an ask immediately follows; preserve unseen-card availability and ordinary stack behavior. If input wins before creation, the chosen skip policy terminally skips the late introduction and handles the ask normally. The unchosen retain alternative keeps pending for the otherwise-eligible new setup and delivers later at usable readiness behind any shown card; in that alternative, the new input and work/cards resulting from it are the explicit exception to the pre-creation activity guard, not permission to welcome older installations or pre-existing activity. No already-committed welcome is discarded merely because an ask arrives. The first accepted main-input turn or welcome-thread reply ends the introductory hint; hint wording stays unchanged.

Ownership and replies: The host presents approved copy through CardService with author Firstmate, not as an app attention card with no reply destination. Firstmate’s next context includes the note’s identity and content without a separate composition wake. Replies take the normal durable captain-turn/about-card path to Firstmate, with existing failure/parking handling. Replying resolves nothing; the card waits offstage for an answer and returns under existing Firstmate thread rules. Revise the same card when the answer changes its contents; otherwise use its thread. Readiness reconciliation never overwrites an authored reply or revision, and no second onboarding persona, crewmate close-out hold or new reply classifier is introduced.

Checkable done criteria: (1) Fresh setup through the relevant key and Claude paths yields the approved welcome and usable input in the first normal ready screen without waiting for inference, demonstrated with held/failing mock inference. (2) Invalid/cancelled setup, empty catalogs, missing clients and pause-only accounts produce no welcome; catalog settlement and pause recovery reconcile correctly. (3) Duplicate updates and crash injection before/after transaction commit produce at most one note/answer record, no consumed-without-card state and no lost pending eligibility. Relaunch restores identity/thread; dismissal and cleanup never recreate. (4) Legacy installations, missing old stamps, prior activity, reconnects and preconfigured starts create no new automatic note; eligible pending setup survives readiness changing while closed. (5) Both input orders, an existing shown card, welcome-thread replies and a storage failure preserve task delivery, drafts, focus, unread cards and the chosen race policy. (6) The exact copy/drawing fits minimum window size and both themes without horizontal overflow or forcing the person to scroll the introduction before starting a task.

Unchanged behavior: Derived setup gate, disabled input/ignored voice while genuinely gated, provider choices and sign-in flow, model/account routing, pause cards, caption fade, existing input-hint words, normal stack priority, unread rules, notifications and ordinary thread mechanics. Diagnostics disclosure/events remain independent and once-only; created is not a new read event.

Scope exclusions: No tour, coach marks, sample work, project registration or clone, forge sign-in, personalization prompt, new permission request, paid inference probe, redesigned stack, general retry subsystem or automatic “welcome back”. The subsequent build updates docs/first-launch.md and the design skill’s first-launch account, including the earlier live-authorship decision, creation-time semantics and chosen race policy; it respects the settings/cards/tasks/feed single writers and avoids a welcome-specific runner or second store.

Explicit assumptions: Once means per app-data profile, not person/account; release and development profiles remain separate. Intentional app-data reset starts anew. Older installations do not need missed-welcome repair; preconfigured never-gated starts remain excluded. Local serving facts suffice without a live success guarantee. Approved fixed copy replaces the previous live-authorship policy while preserving one Firstmate voice and the narrowly scoped informational-note exception. The diagram describes default panel positions as work begins, not forced panel visibility. The original two numbered choices were marked unresolved in the proposal; the persisted selections orientation and skip settle them. There are no dependent questions in this round.

Recommended tests: Extend src/core/firstRun.test.ts and persistence/migration tests through real service interfaces for fresh/legacy/prebound/pending cases, model/account eligibility, settled availability, pause recovery, duplicate callbacks, obsolete welcome wakes and transaction failure/crash recovery. Extend src/core/orchestrator/cardService.test.ts, firstmateAgent.test.ts, crewSupervisor.test.ts and src/renderer/src/app/store.test.ts for recorded ownership/context, both input orders, welcome-thread return, dismissal/reopening guards and stack/focus behavior. A focused rendering test independently owns exact approved copy and labels; source-string presence tests are not evidence. Update tests/e2e/first-launch.spec.ts and affected card-threads/card-containment callers through shared helpers, with every named test owning prerequisites or the deliberate ordered first-launch journey consolidated as one test. Use disposable HOME/userData and existing mock provider/Claude client, never real credentials. Collect a ready-screen picture, ordered readiness/commit/render/input events, request counts proving no welcome inference, and persisted identity before/after restart and dismissal. Assert order/work rather than guessed wall-clock windows. The build gate is pnpm typecheck && pnpm check && pnpm lint:adherence && pnpm test; then pnpm build and the affected Playwright files/cases (confirm lanes, use the actual lane and --no-deps for renderer/application specs), plus pnpm replay:gate when changing the prompt/card contract/routing/card surface. Run affected named cases alone and then complete files.
